Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
As informed by learnedState Law Officer, notice to the informant has been served on 20.03.2025 but none is present to press this application.

2. Heard Sri Jitendra Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Amit Kumar, learned State Law Officer for the State and also perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 74 of 2024 under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5(j)(ii)/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Vishungarh, District Kannauj during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The victim herein is the deponent of the instant bail application.

sentences.text: She was found pregnant at the time of recovery.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
5. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant-Sani Kumar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
8. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

9. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
